purpose: Queryable claim-to-evidence and follow-up map; interpretations are not established causal mechanisms.

claims.question: Can better input histories make the same demonstrated actions easier to learn?
claims.finding: Successes change 1 to 14, 2 to 13, and 3 to 17 out of 32 at matched answers and update counts.
claims.unit: 16 distinct goal identities; repeated fits, recipe worlds and attempt seeds.
controls: 366 identical action targets and 8,820 target tokens
23 updates; batch target-token counts and initialization matched
additional training and randomized valid query ordering
limits: Input length and total computation differ.
Copyability, recency and relevant information are not isolated.
Not clearly better than discovery teaching.
Specific repair pending in a second model family.
claims.decision: Prioritize accepted second-family repair; then untouched goal/world and consistent item-name controls.

claims.question: Does code that fills observed recipe arguments improve completion?
claims.finding: Discovery-trained actors improve 323 to 381 successes out of 768 paired attempts; 74 gains, 16 losses.
claims.unit: 48 distinct goals, four worlds, two training seeds, two attempt seeds.
controls: Same weights in each interface pair
No extra materials or host-chosen quantities
limits: Code repairs execution, not demonstrated learned planning.
Some attempts are harmed.
Remaining stock/ordering problems are not resolved.
Not a new general concept of programmatic assistance.
claims.decision: Measure model learning separately from host execution; retain whole-goal and resource costs.

claims.question: Do fixed RL updates improve other crafting goals?
claims.finding: Raw warm/RL1/RL2/extraSFT1: 4/4/5/4 of 16. Assisted warm/RL1/RL2/extraSFT1: 5/4/4/5 of16.
claims.unit: Eight repeatedly examined diagnostic B goals, each sampled twice; official TRAIN roots, shared recipe world.
controls: Real checkpoint updates and native outcomes verified
384 small receipt bindings for eight readout cells
limits: One added raw success on one attempt.
One-step SFT is not dose/data/compute matched to two-step RL.
B is not an untouched test and must not select training or checkpoints.
claims.decision: Finish accepted bounded sequence; do not extend unchanged RL by default or choose the favorable B checkpoint.

claims.question: Do sampled attempts provide useful within-goal reward differences?
claims.finding: Four training goals fail in all 64 attempts across two rounds and both interfaces; their direct relative advantage is zero. Only 21.5–28.6% of generated tokens receive nonzero relative credit across collections.
claims.unit: Eight A goals; four samples per goal per collection.
controls: Raw and assisted models differ after round one
limits: Shared-parameter learning can affect zero-credit goals.
Does not prove all sparse-reward RL fails or updates are large enough.
Improved sampling experience and reward shaping are separate interventions.
claims.decision: Prioritize A-only recovery demonstrations versus ordinary examples; assess full-start A completion before a fresh transfer test.

claims.question: Has RL ever improved these models?
claims.finding: An early root pilot improved 5 to 16 of 24; news helper improved 422 to 437 or 436 of 512. Stronger controls weakened broader claims.
claims.unit: Six root compositions of familiar helper questions; separate fixed classification panels.
limits: Root checkpoint selection and prior exposure.
Broader fixed root readout only 13 to 16 of 48.
Fresh news RL427/429 versus extraSFT426 of512, uncertain difference.
Improved helpers did not consistently improve whole-task roots.
claims.decision: Preserve positive results; claim task-local learning, not a general RL or recursive-architecture advantage.

claims.question: Can isolated local judgments improve a whole selection answer?
claims.finding: One helper per candidate after Python organization improved 10 to 22 of 24 complete answers.
claims.unit: Twelve fresh selection cases, two sampling seeds.
limits: Programmed decomposition, not learned routing or recursion depth.
About 3.7 times input tokens.
Confidence-selected partial refinement did not reliably recover the full effect.
claims.decision: Reserve selective information views as a longer-term direction; require budget-matched simple baselines.

claims.question: Do learned question plans and helpers beat simpler full-context answering?
claims.finding: Fresh MuSiQue direct/SFT-plan/RL-plan 54/53/56 of128; Hotpot direct/planned152/151 of256. Plan-only controls often match at roughly one-third tokens.
claims.unit: 64 MuSiQue and128 Hotpot parent questions, repeated twice.
limits: Question-list pipeline, not arbitrary Python RLM recursion.
Final reader can use original full source directly.
Does not show decomposition never helps other tasks.
claims.decision: Do not expand this same full-context QA setup without a task that requires useful intermediate information or action.

claims.question: Does code evaluation help when the model still chooses the arithmetic expression?
claims.finding: Numeric FinQA direct/code:51/108 of508 for4B,52/102 for8B; one call each and less than1% added total tokens.
claims.unit: 508 prior-exposed numeric question IDs, with repeated source documents.
controls: Looser post-hoc numeric tolerance retains direction
limits: Known units, rounding and gold execution defects.
Not official FinQA accuracy or independent-document replication.
Established program-aided arithmetic, not new method.
Semantic paired-win/loss audit not completed.
claims.decision: Retain as recovered evidence; audit paired semantic gains before another training branch or a paper claim.

claims.question: When does a helper help the original goal?
claims.finding: Native children solved some assigned subtasks; every parent in the short screen reached its cap before the full outcome was known.
limits: Unknown parent outcomes are not ordinary terminal failures.
Planned complete-goal pilot is one goal and two attempts per arm.
Routing currently programmed, not learned.
claims.decision: Finish existing budget-matched whole-goal pilot before deeper recursion or learned routing.

claims.question: Does making more state information visible necessarily improve planning?
claims.finding: Recipe notebook and demand-table pilots did not rescue deeper crafting tasks; household command gains were confined to two games.
claims.unit: Small exploratory panels; demand-table0/8 versus0/8, not equivalence.
limits: Tiny panels do not prove no useful design exists.
More failed-attempt efficiency is not better completion.
Flat zero bootstrap interval is degenerate.
claims.decision: Retire unchanged displays for now; test actionable recovery and complete-goal utility instead.
